                    ### Question
                    A father brings his 3-year-old son to the pediatrician because he is concerned about his health. He states that throughout his son's life he has had recurrent infections despite proper treatment and hygiene. Upon reviewing the patient's chart, the pediatrician notices that the child has been infected multiple times with S. aureus, Aspergillus, and E. coli. Which of the following would confirm the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Negative nitroblue-tetrazolium test
opb. Normal dihydrorhodamine (DHR) flow cytometry test
opc. Positive nitroblue-tetrazolium test
opd. Increased IgM, Decreased IgG, IgA, and IgE
ope. Increased IgE and IgA, Decreased IgM

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most likely cause of this patient's symptoms is hyper-IgE syndrome, suggested by the pattern of Increased IgE and IgA, Decreased IgM. This is in line with the patient's recurrent infections with S. aureus, Aspergillus, and E. coli. A positive nitroblue-tetrazolium test, which would confirm chronic granulomatous disease, is not the most likely cause based on the presented information.
